newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soap opera trial due to stage final act.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soap opera trial due to stage final act.

text.p: The final act of a sensational murder case involving Brazilian soap opera actors will begin on Wednesday when the former wife of a television star goes on trial for the murder of his screen lover.

Male-stripper-turned-TV-star Guilherme de Padua, 27, was convicted in January of the murder of his co-star Daniela Perez. The body of the 22-year-old actress was found on a Rio roadside with 16 stab wounds in December 1992.
The actor's former wife Paula Thomaz, 23, was charged jointly with the actor, but maintains she is innocent. Her trial begins on Wednesday, a court official said on Tuesday.

Padua originally confessed to the crime, saying Perez had been hounding him to have sex with her. But later he accused his ex-wife of murdering the actress out in a fit of jealousy, stabbing Perez at least 15 times with a pair of scissors.
The actor said he had an affair with Perez because her mother, Gloria, was the script writer for the soap opera and it was in his interest to keep her happy.

The case has become Brazil's equivalent to the O.J. Simpson trial in the United States. It has dragged on for almost five years, littered with interviews by the defendants from behind bars, conflicting testimony from limelight-seeking witnesses and angry calls for justice from the victim's family.

Millions of Brazilian soap opera fans have watched its twists and turns as closely as they followed the soap opera, "De Corpo e Alma" (Of Body and Soul), in which Padua shot to fame as the brooding lover of sexy Yasmin, played by Perez.
The Thomaz trial seemed likely to attract the same torrent of media publicity as the trial of her former husband.
Padua was sentenced to 19 years in jail, of which he has already served four while awaiting trial.
Thomaz faces 12 to 30 years in prison if found guilty.
